answer: Agents secure network roles by solving 1,000 unique computational units as a baseline. An honest agent pays once, but an attacker must incur 1,000 times the cost for fakes. A verifier monitors the falcon-patterned execution trace of each agent. It probes the inlet of local data buffers; if an agent shares memory across a canyon of parallel tasks, it treats this redundancy as evidence of a sybil clone. Such leaks trigger an immediate identity burn and asset forfeiture.
